system.summary: Two-digit number for each letter of the 27-letter Spanish alphabet (A=34 ... D=37, E=01 ... Z=23, Ñ=11), used for names and key words inside letters in clear.
system.notes: Broken by Narváez (2015). The table is ../key.tsv (argumedo1921), applied unchanged. Writer's slips are mostly one code off (34/35/36/37, 01/05, 10/12, 15/12, 02/12).

prior_solution.where: Narváez 2015 (pp. 117-122) and 2019 (pp. 358-364, read from photographs of a loan copy) break the table on the 5 and 20 Oct 1921 letters only (targets/argumedo1921) and say it reads 'otras de ese autor' without naming them; these eight letters are not named or read in print. Period decipherment slips exist in the fonds for six of them (DCXXI.3.306.1; DCXXI.4.425.2 image .0001), found after decoding.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling asked for the Narváez leads to be pushed and decided on the use of the CEHM-Carso images with AI readers (25 Nov 2026); AI models (Claude) transcribed (twice, one blind), applied the published table, read and checked. No person has checked the transcription or the reading.

solution.what: CEHM catalogue search 'Argumedo' in fondo DCXXI: 59 records; Argumedo letters with runs beyond argumedo1921 listed; images fetched from the viewer.
147 runs of seven letters transcribed twice (T1; T2 blind by a second model), hashed before decoding; 1,591 of 1,599 pair places agree; differences settled on the image without the decode.
C1: the frozen table on Narváez's ten printed runs (2019 pp. 359-363): 87 of 89 letters (0.978), pass mark 0.95.
C2: Spanish trigram score of all new runs, frozen table -2.669 against 1,000 permutations of the code values (best -4.590); none at or above.
All runs marked word by word with strict marks (reading_marked.tsv, 25 Nov 2026 19:40 EST): 283 cipher words, 256 read, 27 holes (0.905). count_words.py passes.

After decoding: period decipherment slips DCXXI.3.306.1 (13 images, stamps matching the letters) found and compared: they gloss five of the seven letters run by run, give the intended word at 20 of the 27 holes, and differ in six places where both transcriptions agree on the figures.

Blind second reading of the period slips DCXXI.3.306.1 by a helper AI agent that saw neither the first slip reading nor the decode (25 Nov 2026 21:47-21:54 EST; period_slips_DCXXI.3.306.1_blind.tsv): every slip word at the six divergences is confirmed; the two slip readings differ at ten places that bear on no count (listed in NOTES.md).

Round 2, frozen plan round2/PLAN.md (hashed 25 Nov 21:54:49 EST): the five later Argumedo letters checked for runs; only DCXXI.4.425.2 has them (20 runs). Blind T2 (25 Nov 21:55-21:59 EST) and T1 (27 Nov 18:52-18:54 EST) hashed before decoding; 19 of 20 runs agree, the other settled on the image.
Round 2 C2: trigram score of the 20 runs of DCXXI.4.425.2, frozen table -3.089 against 1,000 permutations (seed 20261126; best -4.245); none at or above.

DCXXI.4.425.2 read with strict marks: 47 cipher words, 43 read, 4 holes (0.915). Its period slip (image .0001), compared afterwards, fits except PABLO ARIZA/'Pancho Ariza' and DON PABLO/'don Pancho' (run 7).

The runs placed in their sentences from the images (reading_<letter>.md, an AI helper, 19:03-19:13 EST) and translated sentence by sentence with the same holes (translation_<letter>.md, an AI helper, 19:37-19:41 EST); the counted words unchanged.

Cold check by a separate AI agent that did not build the package: scripts rerun with identical output, an independent decoder agrees on all 167 runs, strict recount 330/299/31, about 45 runs compared with the images (no digit difference); its corrections (doubts list, dates, translation, wording) made.

validation.notes: Planned controls passed: C1 (87/89 letters on Narváez's printed runs; 86/89 if his printed 'L7(sic)' is scored as a miss) and C2 (table above all 1,000 permuted keys) in round 1; C2 again in round 2 (DCXXI.4.425.2). The period slips, compared after decoding, differ in meaning in eight places; spellings and additions are listed in the slip files.

outcome.method_basis: Narváez's published table (2015, p. 122; 2019, p. 363), applied unchanged to eight letters he did not discuss (the table in ../key.tsv). The period slips (DCXXI.3.306.1; DCXXI.4.425.2 image .0001) were compared after decoding and not used for the reading or the counts.
outcome.fraction_read_source: All cipher words of the eight letters: 330, of which 299 read as the key gives them and 31 holes (writer's slips, codes outside the table, open overstrikes). Round 1 (seven letters) 256 of 283; round 2 (DCXXI.4.425.2) 43 of 47.

texts.label: Argumedo to Félix Díaz, 1921-09-09
texts.summary: Money for the rescue of Gral. Vicente Benítez; Rafael Delgado, Hermenegildo Heredia, Aurelio C. García; the belligerency memorial of Lic. Del Villar; the Colegio Militar cadets.

texts.label: Argumedo to Félix Díaz, 1921-12-26
texts.summary: Railwaymen and wireless sets for the coming campaign; strikes and divisions; Dr. Arturo de la Fuente in the State of Mexico; Pimentel, Castillo, Ariza, Enríquez de Rivera, Pancho C. González; Oaxaca; new keys.

texts.label: Argumedo to Félix Díaz, 1922-01-26
texts.summary: Charles Bounellie (Moneglia?) authorised to receive war material in Michoacán; a letter from San Antonio via Ernesto Argaiz for Gral. Sánchez Díaz; Carlos M. Peralta and the 1913 ticket.

texts.label: Argumedo to Félix Díaz, 1922-02-05
texts.summary: Esteban Cantú's manifesto; Enrique Estrada and M. Caraveo preparing a defection and a provisional presidency.

texts.label: Argumedo to Félix Díaz, 1922-03-25
texts.summary: Orders and documents delivered; a meeting with don Pablo Ariza to raise funds; a journey to Puebla, Isauro and Fidencio López, Guadalajara; Governor Badillo and the police inspector Col. Francisco Pérez; Toluca and Zitácuaro; Dr. de la Fuente; Escobar's 'obra de disolución'.

texts.label: Argumedo to Félix Díaz, 1922-04-10
texts.summary: Orders and documents delivered; demands for money (fifty armed men, $20,000); Pimentel organiser in Oaxaca; Gral. Ismael Hernández; Mario Ferrer's manifesto.

texts.label: Argumedo to Félix Díaz, 1922-06-09
texts.summary: Sixty armed men and $500 for Gral. Agustín Ramírez via Dr. de la Fuente (Toluca, Mixquiahuala); De la Huerta in New York; Pimentel to Oaxaca.

gaps.item: 26 holes that are writer's slips or codes outside the table (reading_marked.tsv, round2/reading_marked.tsv)
gaps.detail: Seen on the image: one-code slips, codes 30 and 55 outside the table, two dropped letters (ENRRIQU{-/E}Z, ANTONI{-/O}); the key does not give the word as written and no clear copy of the letters is known; 20 are given by a period slip (probable), 6 have no other witness.

gaps.item: 5 open overstrikes: GONZ{A?/A}LEZ, L{O?/O}S, ARGUME{D?/D}O, HG{F?/O} (round 1), PERSE{I?/G}UIRA (4.425.2)
gaps.detail: Two figures typed or written over each other; 3 are given by a period slip (probable); listed in NOTES.md Transcription doubts.
